title: Devtooling first-run cheatsheet + onboarding sprint notes
content:
Goal:
- Produce a short, pragmatic first-run cheatsheet + minimal quickstart that a backend engineer can follow in ~10 minutes to call Redwood from local dev and iterate locally on prompts and telemetry.
- Deliverables for sprint: cheatsheet doc, 3 language snippets (py/node/go), local emulator recipe, 1 ‘playground’ template repo, one CLI flow for token/cost preview.

Audience and persona:
- Software engineers (backend/frontend) who need to prototype Redwood API usage quickly.
- Platform/solutions engineers who will embed the SDK into microservices.
- Customer engineering pairing sessions (fast ramp checklist).

Non-goals:
- Exhaustive SDK reference (that lives in API docs).
- Full security/compliance guide — link to product security page instead.

Design constraints / guiding principles:
- Minimal friction: default should ‘just work’ without env setup beyond an API key and docker.
- Cross-language parity: examples in Python, Node, Go should match behavior and outputs.
- Small surface area: provide 5 canonical examples (text gen, chat, embeddings, streaming, rerank).
- Observable by default: include a minimal telemetry hook (event names + sample logs).

First-run path (happy path) — 6 steps (10 min):
1) Create free account / copy API key (assume users have it).
2) Clone the template repo: `git clone github.com/redwood/devtooling/first-run-template`
3) Run local emulator (optional): `docker compose up --profile emulator` (starts a lightweight proxy that records requests)
4) Install local SDK + run quick example: `pip install redwood-dev` then `python quickstart.py` or `npm i @redwood/dev && node quickstart.js`
5) Inspect request/response in the local emulator UI or log at http://localhost:8080
6) Run the token-cost preview: `rw-cli preview --model redwood-v1 --prompt "Summarize X" --max-tokens 128`

Cheatsheet commands (copy/paste):
- Clone: `git clone git@github.com:redwood/devtooling.git && cd devtooling/first-run-template`
- Start emulator: `docker compose up --detach emulator`
- Python quickstart: `python examples/python/quickstart.py`
- Node quickstart: `node examples/node/quickstart.js`
- Go quickstart: `go run examples/go/quickstart.go`
- CLI token preview: `rw-cli preview --model redwood-compact --prompt-file examples/prompt.txt --max-tokens 64`

Minimal code snippets (representative):
- Python (sync):
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  resp = client.generate(model="redwood-v1", prompt="Explain recursion in 3 lines")
  print(resp.text)

- Node (async):
  const { Client } = require('@redwood/dev')
  const c = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const out = await c.generate({ model: 'redwood-v1', prompt: 'List best practices for caching' })
  console.log(out.text)

- Go (minimal):
  c := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  out, _ := c.Generate(context.Background(), redwood.GenerateParams{Model: "redwood-v1", Prompt: "Short haiku about devloops"})
  fmt.Println(out.Text)

Streaming example (how we recommend demonstrating):
- Use the emulator and the SDK streaming API. Provide a tiny demo page that consumes SSE and appends to a textarea. Keep streaming example under 50 lines in the template.

Telemetry and logs (what to capture):
- Event names (recommended): `devx.first_run.started`, `devx.example.executed`, `devx.preview_cost.used`, `devx.emulator.playback`
- Minimum payload fields: event, timestamp, sdk_version, model, route, latency_ms, success_bool
- Example log line: `INFO devx.example.executed model=redwood-v1 route=/generate latency_ms=120 success=1 sdk=python/0.12.0`
- Note: do NOT collect user prompt text by default. If user enables enhanced telemetry, make it opt-in and document retention.

Local emulator design notes (short):
- Runs as a tiny proxy that can: (a) forward traffic to hosted API, (b) record request/response, (c) provide a replay UI and token estimation.
- Implementation approach: docker compose with a small Go binary (single static binary) + SQLite for recordings. Keep installation < 20MB compressed.
- Use case: offline demos, demo capture for support, deterministic replay for evaluation.

Docs checklist for the cheatsheet page:
- [ ] Short 1-paragraph overview + who it’s for
- [ ] One-liner install and run commands (copy/paste)
- [ ] 3 language snippets + streaming example
- [ ] Emulator quickstart + how to inspect logs
- [ ] Token cost preview instructions + sample outputs
- [ ] Troubleshooting section with 5 common errors
- [ ] Links: API reference, security page, pricing table, template repo

Troubleshooting (top 5 quick fixes):
- Missing API key: remind to export REDWOOD_API_KEY or pass `--api-key`
- Connection refused: `docker compose ps` — ensure emulator is up or that dev host allows outbound to api.redwood.ai
- Rate limit 429s: show how to reduce max_tokens and enable caching
- Streaming stalls: check proxy (emulator) buffer settings and server-sent-event support in client
- Cost preview mismatch: explain model variant differences (v1 vs compact) and tokenization edge cases

Rollout plan (rough timeline for the sprint):
- Week 1: finalize cheatsheet text, produce template repo, implement Python/Node examples
- Week 2: build emulator PoC, add Go example, add streaming demo page, internal demo to Solutions Eng
- Week 3: iterate on wording, add telemetry opt-in, ship `rw-cli preview` minimal feature, user testing with 3 partner teams

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should the emulator include a UI by default or be headless with an optional web UI? (tradeoff: complexity vs usefulness)
- Do we include pre-built prompt templates or keep templates generic? (legal/compliance check for prompt retention)
- Exact telemetry schema — need sign-off from security/privacy.

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: draft cheatsheet and create template repo skeleton (ETA: 2025-02-19)
- Marco: PoC emulator binary + docker compose (ETA: 2025-02-26)
- Priya: Node/Python example parity + streaming demo (ETA: 2025-02-26)
- Samir: implement rw-cli preview stub and token estimator (ETA: 2025-03-05)

Meeting notes (paired with Solutions Eng 2025-02-14):
- Feedback: customers want quick toggles to test quantized/compact vs high-quality models and immediate cost comparison; include a small UI for that in the template repo.
- Action: add `--model-toggle` in CLI preview and quick web playground page.

References and links:
- Confluence: DEVEX-1234 (onboarding strategy)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood/devtooling (template repo)
- Jira: DX-78 (emulator), DX-79 (rw-cli preview)
- Slack thread: #devx-onboarding (useful screenshots attached)

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep examples under 40 LOC each.
- Prioritize copy that reduces cognitive load: “What to run now” > architecture paragraphs.
- When in doubt, mirror curl examples to make debugging easiest for non-JS folks.

END OF DRAFT

Unresolved: need legal/infra signoff for telemetry schema before shipping default telemetry.
